findings.issue: Baseline bootstrap images/settings could survive an accepted policy switch and overwrite newer mailbox input or settings on READY.
findings.fix: Reject policy changes while any bootstrap request is buffered.

findings.issue: Invalid integral source IDs 0/negative were treated as unrelated responses, retaining an occupied worker slot until watchdog recovery.
findings.fix: Pass all invalid source IDs to ordinary protocol rejection/accounting; mismatched valid positive IDs remain rejected without releasing another request.

independentBootstrapWitness.error: Drain all bootstrap requests before changing mailbox policy
Drain all bootstrap requests before changing mailbox policy

reviewedInvariants: One physical frame per worker and one global waiting frame
Immediate refill after output/accounting, without another browser capture tick
Monotonic successful source delivery across workers
Reconnect preserves physical old-epoch occupancy until its actual completion
Settings/compile invalidate waiting input; worker exit excludes dead process before refill
Policy changes require fully drained workers and bootstrap queue
App drain stops capture before closing old channel and waits for encode/worker/input quiet
App measurements preserve separate input/receive/main-RAF/projector boundaries and save source ordering/worker telemetry/RTC evidence
limitations: No live GPU, WAN or complete app result is established by this review.
Waiting input has no TTL; a stopped sender during a long compile can leave an old input that dispatches afterward.
Source-less error/drop acknowledgements rely on the current worker emitting exactly one acknowledgement for its sole occupied request.
Initial about:blank drain needs ready workers and a generated /debug compileStartedAt field (or externally established idle compilation); original production /debug omits that field.
App encode timestamp excludes audio acquisition and prior canvas copy; GL submissions are not physical display presentation.
